subsystems.name: Planner / reasoning core
subsystems.role: turns a goal into an ordered set of steps and decides what to do next.
parts: model router for cheap vs capable calls

subsystems.name: Tool and connector layer
subsystems.role: gives the agent hands: typed calls into the software it must operate.
parts: screen-level automation for legacy apps without APIs

subsystems.name: Memory and state
subsystems.role: remembers the goal, the documents behind decisions and what has already been done.
parts: retrieval index over policies and records

subsystems.name: Execution runtime
subsystems.role: runs the agent's actions safely and resumably.

subsystems.name: Guardrails and oversight
subsystems.role: keeps a probabilistic system inside permitted behaviour.
parts: deterministic policy checks before irreversible actions
allowlists of domains, actions and amounts

subsystems.name: Evaluation and observability
subsystems.role: measures whether the agent actually works, and why it failed.
parts: traces of prompts, tool calls and results
regression tests run before each model change

buildSteps.title: Map the workflow
buildSteps.detail: Watch people do the job and record it: inputs, systems touched, decision points, exception paths and what 'done' means. Agents fail on the steps nobody wrote down.

buildSteps.title: Define the tools
buildSteps.detail: Wrap each system action as a typed call with a strict input schema — fetch invoice, update record, send email. For software with no API, capture click paths instead and treat the user interface as the interface.

buildSteps.title: Build the knowledge base
buildSteps.detail: Load the policies, price lists and past cases the decisions depend on into a retrieval index that returns citations, so the agent's reasoning can be traced to a source.

buildSteps.title: Write the orchestration loop
buildSteps.detail: The model proposes an action, the runtime validates and executes it, and the result is fed back for the next step. Loop until the goal is met, a limit is hit, or confidence falls below a threshold.

buildSteps.title: Make it durable
buildSteps.detail: Checkpoint state after every step so a crash, a multi-day approval or a rate-limit pause can resume without redoing work or repeating a payment.

buildSteps.title: Sandbox and scope permissions
buildSteps.detail: Run the agent in a throwaway container with credentials that can only reach the systems and records the task needs, never a general-purpose account.

buildSteps.title: Add deterministic guardrails
buildSteps.detail: Hard-code the rules that must never be broken — maximum payment, no external email, no deletion — outside the model, where reasoning cannot talk its way past them.

buildSteps.title: Evaluate and harden
buildSteps.detail: Replay a suite of recorded real tasks after every prompt or model change, then watch production traces for silent failure modes such as confidently wrong data entry.

prerequisites.tech: LLMs with reliable structured tool calling
prerequisites.why: function and tool calling became a standard API feature from 2023, letting a model emit machine-checkable actions rather than prose.
interleaving thought with action (as in the ReAct line of work) is what turns a chatbot into something that can act on results.
long multi-step jobs need checkpointing and retries, already solved for conventional back-office automation.
interfaces such as the Model Context Protocol and OpenAPI descriptions exist, but coverage across enterprise software is uneven.

prerequisites.tech: Identity, permissions and evaluation for non-deterministic systems
prerequisites.why: there is still no settled way to give an agent a scoped identity or to certify that a probabilistic workflow is safe to run unattended.
much corporate software has no usable API, so robotic process automation remains the fallback interface.

pathway.milestone: single-domain assistants that draft and prepare work while a person approves each action
pathway.unlocks: measured time savings in support, finance operations and back-office processing.

pathway.milestone: task-level autonomy inside one function, with full audit trails and replayed evaluation suites
pathway.unlocks: agents trusted with defined workloads end to end, such as reconciliation or claims triage.

pathway.milestone: standard agent identities, scoped permissions and cross-vendor hand-offs
pathway.unlocks: workflows that span several companies' systems without a human relaying information.

pathway.milestone: long-horizon operations supervised by exception rather than by step
pathway.unlocks: accountability shifts from checking each action to auditing outcomes, which is the real barrier rather than model capability.
